qs.q: Which medication has greatly improved the prognosis of atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome by targeting the complement system?
o: Adalimumab immunosuppressive agent for autoimmune inflammatory conditions
Rituximab targeted immunotherapy against CD20-positive B cells
Infliximab biological treatment directed against tumor necrosis factor
Eculizumab monoclonal antibody therapy targeting the complement system
qs.e: Eculizumab, a monoclonal anti-terminal complement complex antibody, has greatly improved the prognosis of atypical HUS. Other biologic agents listed are not targeted at terminal complement complexes for this indication.

qs.q: Dense deposit disease, a form of membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis, is characterized by dysregulation of the complement system. Which specific complement component is typically found at significantly reduced levels in the serum of affected individuals?
qs.e: Dense deposit disease is defined by the uncontrolled activation and consumption of the alternative complement pathway, leading to markedly decreased levels of serum C3. Reduced C4 levels would suggest activation of the classical or lectin pathways, which are not the primary drivers in this condition.

qs.q: Which of the following is NOT true regarding the complement system? Options
o: Complement attracts phagocytes to both foreign material and healthy self-cells.
Binding mannose-binding lectins to a bacterial capsule initiates the complement cascade.
Complement binds bacteria, forming pores that disrupt their membranes.
Complement proteins eliminate antibody-antigen complexes and prevent damage to host tissues.
Complement consists of serum proteins that activate sequentially, amplifying the immune response.
qs.e: Complement components attract phagocytes to foreign material and pathogens, but they should NOT attract phagocytes to healthy self-cells. The complement system is designed to distinguish self from non-self.

qs.q: The complement system is a crucial part of innate immunity. Which pathway is activated by antigen-antibody complexes?
qs.e: The classical pathway of complement activation is primarily triggered by the binding of C1q to antibody-antigen complexes (typically IgM or IgG) or directly to pathogen surfaces.

qs.q: Which of the following is NOT a primary function of the complement system?
qs.e: While complement components can enhance antigen presentation by B cells, the complement system itself does not directly present antigens to T cells. Its primary functions include lysis, opsonization, and promoting inflammation/chemotaxis.
